result.title: Is the Platform Part of the Measurement? A Protocol and Simulation Study for Cross-Platform Equivalence of Machine-Labelled Policy Sentiment
result.comment: 25 pages, 12 figures, 2 tables. Includes an original 500-replication simulation study. Code: https://github.com/asadfix/platform-measurement (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23105129)
result.summary: Comparing machine-labelled sentiment across social media platforms is now routine: differences in classifier scores between platforms are read as differences in public opinion. These comparisons rest on an assumption that the classifier measures the same construct, on the same scale, on every platform. Some studies check a classifier's validity platform by platform, but to our knowledge none has modelled the platform as a facet of the classifier's measurement. We adapt the psychometric equivalence toolkit (generalizability theory, measurement invariance and differential item functioning, and score linking) to machine-labelled policy sentiment, treating the platform as a survey mode, and specify a six-step protocol with anchor events fixed in advance, an anchor-density audit, and a two-classifier convergence control. A simulation with known ground truth illustrates what the assumption can cost in one generating configuration fixed in advance: across 500 replications, because the platforms measure through different functions, a pooled index that takes platform scores at face value reports the wrong sign of aggregate sentiment on nearly a quarter of days, whereas an index adjusted with each platform's known measurement function does so on under one day in sixty on average. A case study of the instrument from the first author's MSc dissertation, a fine-tuned BERT classifier over 255,446 UK economic-policy comments from Twitter/X, Reddit, YouTube, and Quora, motivates the design and illustrates the instrument-dependence the protocol addresses. The full four-platform application, under fresh collection with the pre-specified design, is the designated follow-up study. The protocol lets a researcher test whether pooling platforms is defensible in a given corpus, or whether platform scores must be linked before any average is taken.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把「平台」视为分类器测量的一个 facet，借用心理测量学的等价工具（概化理论、测量不变性/DIF、分数链接）提出六步协议，并用 500 次重复的已知真值仿真说明不做事先链接的合并指数会在近四分之一天数上报出错误的总体情感符号，另以一个跨 Twitter/X、Reddit、YouTube、Quora 的 BERT 政策情感分类器为案例。
AI.relevance_reason: 其测量等价与分数链接框架可能为 LVR 的可核查线索：判断同一 latent 读出或探针在不同模态、数据集与条件下是否测量同一构念，并把分数方差归因于平台、任务等 facet，而非直接研究视觉推理本身。
